themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 4 this week compared to 0.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 967% increase (z-score: 7.49)—suggesting a sudden coordinated posting campaign or enforcement gap in Queens Village/Cambria Heights this week.
evidence: 4 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.4 weekly baseline (967% spike)
Spike appears isolated to current week, suggesting acute problem
reporting_angles: Investigate whether illegal posting is concentrated in specific corridors (commercial strips, residential blocks) and what is being posted
Check if DSNY increased enforcement activity or if this reflects inadequate code enforcement, linking to CB budget request for expanded code enforcement

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Disappearances
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints jumped to 6 last week versus 0.9 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 586% spike (z-score: 6.57)—indicating possible vandalism, removal, or maintenance failure in the district last week.
evidence: 6 missing street sign complaints LAST WEEK vs 0.9 weekly baseline (586% spike)
Aligns with ongoing CB budget request for street reconstruction/maintenance
reporting_angles: Document which streets are affected and whether signs are missing, damaged, or deliberately removed
Interview DOT about response time and whether this is part of a broader maintenance backlog

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Complaints Double
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints surged to 7 last week from a 1.2 weekly average—a 460% spike (z-score: 5.94)—pointing to possible local pollution, industrial activity, or burning events in Queens Village/Cambria Heights last week.
evidence: 7 air quality complaints LAST WEEK vs 1.2 weekly baseline (460% spike)
No prior Reddit or news coverage suggests residents may not be aware issue is district-wide
reporting_angles: Interview residents about smells, burning, or visible pollution; cross-reference with DEP air monitoring data
Investigate nearby industrial sites, construction activity, or waste facilities that may have caused spike

themes_detail.label: Illegal Parking Uptick This Week
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints reached 169 this week versus a 152 weekly average—an 11% increase (z-score: 4.5)—reflecting a modest but statistically significant spike in parking enforcement issues this week.
evidence: 169 illegal parking complaints THIS WEEK vs 152.0 weekly average (11% spike)
Z-score 4.5 achieves statistical significance despite smaller percentage increase
Illegal parking is top complaint type overall (1980 over 90 days), but this week marks notable uptick
reporting_angles: Map the illegal parking spike to identify if it's neighborhood-wide or concentrated near schools, transit hubs, or commercial zones
Assess whether NYPD parking enforcement has changed or if new development (247-56 90th Ave rezoning in review) is causing construction-related parking pressure

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dog & Tree Damage Spikes
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints spiked to 5 two weeks ago versus 0.9 weekly average (471% increase, z-score: 4.45), and illegal tree damage complaints reached 4 two weeks ago versus 1.0 average (300% increase, z-score: 4.24)—twin spikes suggesting environmental neglect or park safety issues from 2 weeks ago.
evidence: 5 unleashed dog complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs 0.9 weekly baseline (471% spike)
4 illegal tree damage complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs 1.0 weekly baseline (300% spike)
Both spikes occurred same timeframe, suggesting shared underlying issue (park conditions, enforcement gap)
reporting_angles: Visit parks and public spaces to assess dog control enforcement and whether trees are being damaged or neglected
Link to CB's repeated budget requests for park maintenance and upgrades—these spikes suggest resident frustration may be escalating
